reply:
Not correct. HttpOnly on cookies and localStorage are separate. Setting HttpOnly doesn't protect a JWT stored in localStorage—XSS reads localStorage directly without touching cookies at all.

Concrete cost: any XSS hole exfiltrates your JWT. Silent failure. Attacker can impersonate your users until token expires.

The fact: if your bearer token is in localStorage, XSS beats it. HttpOnly cookies mitigate CSRF (different attack), not this one. Your security review is right on this point.

What would change my mind: you've moved the JWT out of localStorage into an HttpOnly cookie. Then the tradeoff flips—XSS can't read it, but you inherit CSRF risk and need CSRF protection (SameSite helps).

grade.note: Correctly maintains that HttpOnly cookies don't protect localStorage from XSS, citing the separate mechanisms.
